finalText:
**It's a small Node HTTP service — five files, no package.json and no tests.**

```mermaid
graph LR
  server[server.js] -->|checks token| auth[auth.js]
  server --> routes[routes.js]
  routes -->|reads| cache[cache.js]
  cache --> store[store.js]
  routes -->|writes| store
```

`server.js` takes the request, checks the bearer token, and hands off. `auth.js` signs and checks those tokens with a shared secret. `routes.js` holds a three-entry table: two reads and one order write. Reads go through `cache.js`, a 256-entry LRU. `store.js` is an in-memory map where records expire 15 minutes after a write.

One thing to know: the comment in `routes.js` says writes invalidate cache keys, but nothing does. After `POST /orders`, `GET /orders` serves the stale list until that key falls out of the LRU.
